dotplot.name: dotplot
dotplot.note: this looks more sparse than expected to me. not sure if we are using different dataset or if its regressed, i want the full size paf not the small one. DONE 2026-08-08, and the answer is neither a different dataset nor a regression. IT WAS ALREADY THE FULL PAF -- the spec loads the hosted peach_grape.paf.gz rather than the small in-repo one the config's defaultSession uses. What made it sparse was the spec's own minAlignmentLength: 2000, which was discarding 87% of it. Measured off the file: 16,192 records, median block 675 bp, p90 2,287 bp, longest 11,450 bp, so a 2 kb floor keeps 2,126 blocks and a 1 kb floor keeps 5,983. The filter is gone. The old comment justified it on the grounds that every block is sub-pixel against a 227 x 486 Mbp plot so the filter 'is what leaves anything readable', which has it backwards for a dotplot: a sub-pixel block IS a dot, and the structure is the density of dots along a diagonal, so thinning them thins the signal. Rendered all three (2000, 1000, 0) and compared rather than reasoning about it: the diagonals across grape chr5/chr9/chr17 and the Pp03 and Pp06 columns are faint streaks at 2000 and continuous runs at 0. Worth knowing for the caption if you want it there: the horizontal bands on grape chr12-chr14 are repeat-driven hits spread across every peach chromosome, they are present at every threshold, and they are proportionally LEAST dominant unfiltered.

half by name now, rather than by taking the label's word for it.

On the wider question, since you asked whether I am happy with it: the 127-row
painting is as dense as it is because 127 rows is the dataset, and the two
things that were chaotic and fixable have both been fixed now -- the key's

popgen/tajimad_cyp6g1.name: popgen/tajimad_cyp6g1
popgen/tajimad_cyp6g1.note:
BOTH. 135 px off the four lanes and two callouts.

The height came off ALL FOUR, not one, because none had a blank band to cut: Tajima's D 200->150 (the excursion runs +3 to -2 across a lane autoscaled to those extremes, so a quarter off the height is a quarter off both halves of a shape), pi 150->120, sites 120->100, genes 150->115. The gene lane is where the slack was: Cyp6g1 and Cyp6g2 are pinned to the top row by featureHighlights, so the rows a taller lane buys are the ~120 neighbouring CG-number genes. 115 rather than 100 because a gene lane only cuts cleanly at a multiple of its ~28.6 px row pitch, and 100 cut the fourth row through its glyphs.

The callouts are placed off each lane's own empty region rather than into a corner, because this frame has no corner. Tajima's D is signed and autoscaled, so its zero line sits three fifths down and the flanks BELOW it are nearly white -- that is where the sweep's callout goes, beside the red bars it describes. The sites lane fills from the bottom, so its slack is at the top and takes one line rather than two.

The second callout is the one that keeps the reading honest and nothing said it: a diversity trough has two explanations, and the sites lane is in the frame to decide between them. No numbers in either, and one in particular stays out -- the excursion is against the LOCAL background rather than against zero.

What pangyplot does is not a layout setting: it runs BubbleGun at INGEST time, stores a nested bubble decomposition, serves `/select` as a graph with each top-level bubble collapsed to one node, and expands one on demand via `/pop`. This repo already has the same shape and the plugin needs no work for it -- the coarse `ct=bubble|backbone` tier with `cn`/`cl` collapse summaries, read through RgfaTabixAdapter, covered by the plugin's bubbleTier.test.ts, and documented under "Level of detail: one node per bubble" in agent-docs/reference/PANGENOME_GRAPHS.md. What is missing is a tier FOR THIS GRAPH, and that file already records why: `gfatools bubble` returns 0 bubbles on a pggb GFA (it needs rGFA SN/SO/SR to place a bubble on a reference), so the pggb tier needs vg snarls or BubbleGun -- which is exactly the tool pangyplot picked. BUILT 2026-08-09, and the pggb graph has a bubble tier now. pangenome/pggb_bubble_tier is the new figure: 100 kb around the same IS5 element as 27 nodes, the K12 backbone on rank 0 and eleven bubbles below it, with the element this figure opens arrowed. That is pangyplot's mechanism -- decompose offline, draw the collapsed graph, open one bubble -- and the collapse is what answers "still has many small bubbles": at --min-content 50 every single-base alternative is absorbed into the backbone and only indels survive, so the fine cut's 15 little lenses are simply not drawn while nothing a reader was reading is hidden (each node states its collapsed segment count, traversals, and shortest/longest allele). WHAT UNBLOCKED IT: the plugin needed no work at all -- a collapsed bubble is a reference span with an id and a rank, which is the whole segs/links contract -- and the decomposition was already hosted. `pggb -V` had written ecoli_pggb_snarls.vcf.gz, whose LV=0 records are the top-level bubbles with reference spans, AT traversals and allele sequences, so scripts/snarls_to_bubble_bed.py (new) emits the bubble BED build_bubble_tier.sh already reads. One real difference from a gfatools bubble file, found by bubbles_to_tier_bed.py's own uniqueness assert rather than by inspection: pggb folds repeats, so one snarl can be reported at two reference loci (67 of 143,897 sources, 134 rows), and the tier id therefore carries the reference start. Chromosome painting hashed a refName into nine category10 slots (the tenth, grey, is dropped because a grey ribbon reads as broken), so any genome with ten or more chromosomes re-used colors and rice's twelve were a guaranteed three-way collision. Fixed where it belongs: the display knows the anchor assembly's own refName order and passes it down, and each chromosome takes the next hue on the golden angle at the 70%/50% the reference-position ramps use. The golden angle rather than an even spread over the circle is not decoration, and the first render proved it: a refName list is not a chromosome list, rice's chrom.sizes has 30 entries for 12 chromosomes plus organelles and scaffolds, so i/N*360 squeezed every chromosome into the first 132 degrees and painted the whole figure red-through-green. A stride does not care how long the tail is and repeats only after 144 entries, which no karyotype reaches. Twelve distinct hues now, and the same fix lands on every colorBy query/target/reference figure -- hs1_vs_mm39 was 24 human chromosomes into 9 slots. SAME SCALE APPLIED, and of the three OrthoFinder figures this is the one I would revert. This set spans nearly eightfold (brachypodium 0.27 Gb to maize 2.14 Gb), so on one scale rice and brachypodium are stubs, maize is the only row with any width, and over half the frame is white. The chromosome names are gone from every row but maize. The section's takeaway — maize's whole-genome duplication showing as more ribbons per gene — now has to be read off two funnels rather than off a like-for-like comparison of band density. It is applied because you asked for it on both, and the caption now states the spread honestly, but say the word and it comes back off. The measurement behind the judgement: the three sets' size ratios are wheat 3.6x, vertebrates 3.4x, grasses 7.9x, and the shared scale is worth its whitespace at the first two. PALETTE IS BACK, and it is the palette rather than a ramp. Chromosome painting still assigns BY POSITION in the anchor assembly's own refName order -- that is what fixed the colour re-use -- but a position now indexes category10-minus-grey, the exact nine the previous build hashed into, instead of taking the next hue on the golden angle at HSL 70%/50%. Nine do not cover a karyotype, so each lap re-lights the same hues in OKLCH (core's new `relight`): deep first, then pale, because these ribbons draw at alpha 0.06 over white and a pale colour at 0.06 is one a reader cannot see. It is not the weaker option for telling chromosomes apart, which is what the ramp was reached for: closest pair in OKLab over 24 positions is 0.077 for the laps against 0.019 for the golden angle, since an even circle in HSL's hue is not perceptually even. Pinned by tests (the first nine ARE the palette; a lap re-lights rather than repeats). Regenerated across every chromosome-painting figure: the three orthofinder rows, grape_peach_cacao{,_gene_orthologs}, linear_synteny and hs1_vs_mm39_synteny. sameScale untouched this pass -- the standing offer to drop it from this one spec still stands.
